I have resolved the issue where `has_key`, `has_keys`, and `has_any_keys` lookups on `JSONField` failed to handle numeric keys on SQLite, MySQL, and Oracle.

### Cause
In `HasKeyLookup.as_sql`, the right-hand side key(s) were compiled via `compile_json_path`. When a key consisted of numeric digits (e.g. `"1111"`), `compile_json_path` attempted `int("1111")` which succeeded, causing it to format the key as an array index `[1111]` (e.g. `$[1111]`) instead of a JSON object key (e.g. `$."1111"`).

### Solution
1. Updated `HasKeyLookup.as_sql` in [`django/db/models/fields/json.py`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-uiu_diad/django/db/models/fields/json.py#L196-L203) to ensure target keys checked by `has_key`, `has_keys`, and `has_any_keys` are compiled as object keys (`."1111"`).
2. Updated `KeyTransformIsNull` in [`django/db/models/fields/json.py`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-uiu_diad/django/db/models/fields/json.py#L388-L411) to compile `self.lhs` directly using `self.lhs.preprocess_lhs` and `compile_json_path`, accurately handling both key and array index lookups.
3. Added test coverage in [`tests/model_fields/test_jsonfield.py`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-uiu_diad/tests/model_fields/test_jsonfield.py#L579-L595) for numeric key lookups across `has_key`, `has_keys`, and `has_any_keys`.
